where: the 'This deployment' block inside the three-column register below the rule (identical in kiosk-menu)
finding: In the healthy state the register is declared as three columns and drawn as two with a hole in the middle. 'This deployment' is allotted two of the three columns — 757px — and nothing it holds is wider than 496px, so a 293px band of nothing runs from the deployment text to the third column, from the section headings down to the fact row. The two peer sections then set their bodies at two different measures, ~80 characters on the left and ~58 on the right, which is the same 'these are not peers' tell the round-2 body-size fix was meant to close, moved from size into line length. This is not the settled question of how wide the register is; it is how the register spends the width it has. It costs the reader the sense that the lower half is set: at a squint the page has a diagonal of void running from the empty upper right through the middle of its own reference material.
evidence: kiosk-setup--desktop: h2 'This deployment' box x=256–1013 (lg:col-span-2); widest content in it is the caveat ending x=752 and the service-account value ending x=648. Third column starts x=1045. Empty band x=752–1045 for y=305–612. Left column paragraphs wrap at 496px, right column at 363px, both 12px/ink-400.
direction: Let the block's span follow its content or give the content the span. Either the deployment block sits in one column like its peers and the register reads as three equal columns of reference, or the two-column allowance is actually used — the identifying facts and the re-check reply laid across the width rather than stacked at the left edge. As it stands the widest column is the one with the least in it.

where: the gcloud command block and the gutter between it and the 'If the kiosk still waits' column
finding: The command block is the only filled surface on the page and it is 290px wider than the longest line inside it, so most of it is an empty tinted rectangle. Because it also hangs its padding outside the measure to keep the page's left edge — which was the right fix on the left — its right edge now reaches into the column gutter and stops 20px short of an unrelated column's text. The result is that a panel belonging to the diagnosis appears to run underneath the troubleshooting list, and the one place on the page where two registers meet is the tightest gap in the frame while everything else has 32px or more. A reader scanning the right column reads it against a rectangle that has nothing to do with it.
evidence: kiosk-setup-denied--desktop: pre x=244–1025 (781px wide, -mx-3 on a 757px column); its longest line, the --member flag, ends near x=730. 'A code expires…' begins x=1045, leaving 20px of gutter against a nominal lg:gap-8 of 32px. No other element in the left block passes x=752.
direction: Keep the left bleed and stop the right one: the panel should end at the measure its own lines need, not at the column edge. A code block sized to its content also stops looking half-empty, and it restores a clean gutter between the two registers.

where: the account popover under the header chip — the identity block, 'Sign out', and the single 'Kiosk' row
finding: On the counselor's build the menu has one destination, and it is not what the panel presents. 'Sign out' is the only chromatic object in the panel and it sits above the divider, so the reading order is identity, exit, then the single place you can go; and the destination is set at exactly the lightness already spent on the email address, so nothing separates the thing you can act on from the fact you already knew. Shrinking the exit from a slab to a line answered the reach problem, but in a panel with three destinations the white rows still outweighed it, and in a panel with one they no longer do. A navigation surface whose loudest element is the way out reads as a sign-out panel with an afterthought attached.
evidence: kiosk-menu-counselor--desktop: panel 208×125 at x=816–1024; identity block occupies y=56–137 (76px) and the sole row 'Kiosk' y=141–177 (36px). 'Sign out' is danger-400 14px/500, right-aligned; 'Kiosk' and the email are both ink-200, at 14px and 12px.
direction: Where there is one destination, the destination has to be the subject of the panel. Give it the top of the ramp and pull the identity lines down it — the email is a confirmation, not a headline — so the first read is where you can go and the exit is what it is: the quiet, coloured item you look for on purpose. The admin build, with three rows carrying the weight, does not need this.
